source_text: I am feeling angry because when I got claude-2 to tell claude-4 about this I thought it was going to be used and that it would massively speed things up and they didn't even bother trying it?

fragments.text: I am feeling angry because when I got claude-2 to tell claude-4 about this I thought it was going to be used and that it would massively speed things up and they didn't even bother trying it?

reply_text:
㊥ ("they didn't even bother trying it?") I checked the messages, and it went differently: claude-4 never received the route. claude-2 mentioned it to you once ("so I only name it") and left it out of the bell. What you later sent to claude-4 through claude-2 was the curriculum idea: trace Lean's elaborator to get a checklist of steps. claude-4 did act on that, and claude-3's census is the result. The census tells the port what to rebuild, but the port still has to rebuild each step. So the agents carried out what reached them; the fast route was dropped before anything was sent. Your anger at the outcome is fair, though: the faster option was named and nobody tested it.

㊢ (the sequence, from claude-2's buffer and the job record)
1. claude-2 told you that letting native Lean elaborate and translating its output would change the picture, but that it "breaks the mission's 'do not start from scratch' gate", "so I only name it."
2. The first bell to claude-4 (`invoke-1791121847807-…`) carried token-cost and speed items T1–T3 and S1–S4. It also had the paragraph saying the subset is most of the elaborator, marked as context with no action asked. claude-4's reply covers every item and doesn't mention the route.
3. You answered that compiling a blank file needing the elaborator is Lean's fault. claude-2 then proposed tracing Lean's elaborator to get a checklist, and you said: "not only using lean to verify but to give a more detailed 'curriculum' that makes the whole thing totally procedural. Please tell claude-4." That is what was sent, and what was built.

🈖 (where the two ideas differ) "Use the Lean elaborator" can mean two things. One is to ask Lean what to do and then do it ourselves: the curriculum. The other is to let Lean do the elaborating and translate its result. You meant, or came to mean, the second. The agents heard the first, partly because claude-2's reading of gate 1 had already ruled the second out. Your reading of gate 1 today removes that reason.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I dispatch the test now: Lean's compiled output for two or three failing rows, translated to Python by a throwaway translator, checked against the preregistered expected output, outside mfuton-share, with a bell back to me? If it works, the same message to claude-4 would state the route as an action, quote your reading of gate 1, and include the result.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.text: ("wasting lots of time to satisfy a rule") Mostly yes, with one correction. The time is going into rebuilding Lean's elaborator in Python, because the mission's rules allow only source syntax as the compiler's input. But the better solution is likely, not known: nobody has tested it. claude-2 named the route this morning and set it aside as against the gates, and nobody has run it on even one row. The real failure is that no one spent a single packet checking whether that rule was costing the project its fastest route.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.text: (what's established) As of claude-3's census, 17 of 110 rows matched native Lean. Coercion, projection syntax and about 20 instance classes are still to rebuild. Each step costs several probes of 30–60 minutes. Lean elaborates all 110 rows in 24 seconds, and its compiled output per row is already on disk.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.text: (what isn't established) Whether translating that output gives working Python. Possible obstacles: the runtime primitives it calls (`extern`, `implemented_by`), how Lean objects are represented in Python, and whether Rob's aim of replacing handwritten combinators with compiled ones is still met. Those risks look smaller than rebuilding the remaining elaborator steps, but that's my judgement, not a measurement.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-6
previous_reply_acts.text: (whose fault) The agents followed the rules as written. I'd put it on the coordination layer, claude-4 and claude-2 (and me, reading it today). The census showed the "small subset" assumption was false, and nobody took that back to the rules.
